newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Crisis looming for Belgian government over sex.
newsitem.headline: Crisis looming for Belgian government over sex.

text.p: The Belgian government slid towards crisis on Tuesday as leaders of several parliamentary parties said Deputy Prime Minister Elio Di Rupo might be forced to resign over allegations of having sex with minors.

Di Rupo, a francophone socialist who angrily rejects the accusations which first surfaced in Dutch-language newspapers at the weekend, revealed on Monday that he was the subject of a judicial enquiry.

The party leaders were due to meet later on Tuesday to decide what action to take -- including lifting Di Rupo's immunity from prosecution, which could lead to charges at the Cour de Cassation, Belgium's highest court.
"If he is referred to the Cour de Cassation...it would be difficult for him to retain his position as a deputy prime minister," Paul Tant, CVP parliamentary leader told BRTN radio.
The Flemish CVP Christian Democratic Party is the largest party in the ruling coalition government.
"If the facts are so grave that he needs to be charged then he should resign," a spokesman for the Flemish Socialist Party (SP), another coalition partner, said.
Belgium's centre-left coalition is made up of the francophone and Flemish Christian democratic and socialist parties.
Herman de Croo, leader of the main Dutch-speaking opposition VLD Liberals, who played a leading role in launching the allegations against Di Rupo, said he should quit regardless.
Di Rupo, held in high esteem by Belgian homosexuals, says he has only ever had sexual relations with consenting adults.

The parliamentary process instituted against Di Rupo echoes that of Flemish socialist and NATO secretary general Willy Claes, who was forced to resign as head of the alliance last year when his immunity was lifted in the face of allegations he knew of a party slush fund in the 1980s.
The parliamentary party leaders are likely to decide to set up a committee to examine the allegations against Di Rupo.

Based on that and a hearing with Di Rupo and his lawyers, the committee will then decide whether there are grounds to send a recommendation to the full parliament calling for immunity to be lifted. It is then up to a plenary session to vote.
Political analysts say the government is not under immediate threat, but the key will be whether Flemish and francophone Christian democrats support Di Rupo or quietly back off.

Their failure to support the socialist politician could spell the eventual end of the coalition, at a time when public confidence in the whole political apparatus and in the socialist parties in particular is already at a very low ebb.

Last month 250,000 people took to the streets of Brussels in a march originally called to support parents of missing and murdered children in the paedophile scandal that has rocked Belgium, which turned into a show of public disgust at what is seen as a thoroughly corrupt political and legal system.
